newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian diamond stocks to run out if not refilled.
newsitem.headline: Russian diamond stocks to run out if not refilled.

text.p: Russia's diamond stockpile could run out between March 1998 and September 1998 if not replenished, a source in the Audit Chamber said on Friday, referring to a report completed on the issue in September 1996.
"The report concluded that Russia's diamond reserves, if not replenished, could be practically exhausted in one and a half to two years," said the source, who declined to be identified.

But the source also said the report did not mean that Russia had no diamonds, adding that the government's failure to refill reserves was the result of policy confusion in the aftermath of the breakup of the State Committee for Precious Metals and Stones.
"It (the failure to replenish reserves) was not a question of financing, but of common-sense policies," he said.
The committee, known as Komdragmet, ceased functioning in November 1996 after it was disbanded by President Boris Yeltsin.
The committee was responsible for GosFond reserves. The reserves, now known as Goskhran, are run by the Finance Ministry.

De Beers, which is still seeking a diamond export deal with Russia, stopped all purchases of Russian diamonds on December 31, 1996 when it cancelled an interim pact after Moscow failed to approve or reject a new trade deal.
